answer: A vertex in the task graph anchors each applicant: admission needs a plume of verified work tracing back to it, plus a stake locked for audit. Auditors traverse karst channels and sample work at random; a failed item burns the stake and revokes identities sharing its upstream edges. The k-th fake costs 15 + 0.002k^3 units, since each new vertex needs fresh work and stake while audits intensify with cluster size; 1,000 fakes cost about 501,015,500 units. A device farm fails: one machine cannot fabricate 1,000 work plumes, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its stake.
